status: Planning scenario, not forecast or actual pipeline
formula: annual revenue = programs * robots per program per year * modules per robot * module ASP

segments.label: Robotics OEMs
segments.title: Win a place in the customer’s production design.
segments.buyer: Hardware / motion-control engineering lead, with procurement approval.
segments.need: A repeatable actuator that meets torque, thermal, size and cost requirements.
segments.offer: Paid joint evaluation kits, integration support and a qualified production SKU.
segments.contract: Evaluation purchase order, then engineering statement of work and scheduled component supply.
segments.proof: Customer acceptance tests, design release, origin records and a production purchase order.
segments.expand: More units of the same module, then additional joints and robot programs.
segments.why: Shared modules reduce redesign effort and give the buyer a manufacturing transfer path.

segments.label: AI & research teams
segments.title: Sell usable hardware for the next experiment.
segments.buyer: Robotics research lead, lab manager or applied-AI engineering team.
segments.need: An accessible hand or arm platform that can be integrated, repaired and modified.
segments.offer: Hand / arm development kits, spares, interfaces and paid setup support.
segments.contract: Hardware purchase plus optional integration work. Research purchases do not imply future volume.
segments.proof: A paid delivery and an accepted experimental workflow, followed by a repeat purchase.
segments.expand: Additional rigs, replacement modules and later ROSE workflow pilots.
segments.why: Modular hardware creates a direct feedback channel for engineering and reliability improvements.

segments.label: Automation integrators
segments.title: Deliver a subsystem that fits a customer application.
segments.buyer: Integrator engineering director or a robot OEM working with an end customer.
segments.need: A configurable subsystem with a stable supply path and a clear support boundary.
segments.offer: Configured joint, hand or arm assemblies. Mobile platforms enter after product-specific qualification.
segments.contract: Paid engineering milestones, assembly orders and agreed spares / support terms.
segments.proof: Site acceptance, system-level qualification and a repeatable bill of materials.
segments.expand: Replication across sites and service inventory, then manufacturing capacity and ROSE.
segments.why: FlatHill supplies reusable hardware while the integrator owns application deployment.

commercial_stages.label: 01 Evaluate
commercial_stages.title: Turn interest into a paid hardware evaluation.
commercial_stages.buyer: Robotics OEMs and applied-AI teams with a defined engineering problem.
commercial_stages.deliver: A selected module or development kit, documented interfaces and a test procedure.
commercial_stages.contract: A purchase order for the evaluation hardware, with separately scoped integration support.
commercial_stages.gate: The buyer accepts the engineering results and funds the next integration step.
commercial_stages.measure: Paid evaluations, time to first working integration and accepted test results.

commercial_stages.label: 02 Design in
commercial_stages.title: Become part of the customer’s released design.
commercial_stages.buyer: A buyer that has validated the module and is preparing a product or pilot build.
commercial_stages.deliver: Customer-specific interfaces, a frozen BOM and a pilot production package.
commercial_stages.contract: Engineering milestones, change-control terms and a pilot-lot purchase order.
commercial_stages.gate: The customer approves the design, supplier qualification and production acceptance criteria.
commercial_stages.measure: Design wins, pilot yield, quote-to-order conversion and cost per good unit.

commercial_stages.label: 03 Repeat
commercial_stages.title: Convert design wins into scheduled shipments.
commercial_stages.buyer: OEM production teams and integrators replicating a validated configuration.
commercial_stages.deliver: Qualified modules or assemblies with serial traceability and agreed spares support.
commercial_stages.contract: Scheduled purchase orders or supply agreements with volume, lead-time and quality terms.
commercial_stages.gate: Repeat orders and contribution economics justify dedicated U.S. capacity.
commercial_stages.measure: Repeat-order share, on-time delivery, realized gross margin and warranty returns.

commercial_stages.label: 04 Expand
commercial_stages.title: Sell the workflow and production capacity around the hardware.
commercial_stages.buyer: Existing hardware customers with repeat engineering and manufacturing needs.
commercial_stages.deliver: Validated software workflows and qualified production cells with a clear responsibility boundary.
commercial_stages.contract: Software or service agreements after pilot acceptance. Capacity reservations only against actual demand.
commercial_stages.gate: Customers complete paid workflows and the cells meet quality and unit-economics targets.
commercial_stages.measure: Software renewal, attach rate, engineering hours saved and cell utilization.
